source_evidence.anchor: The sum S_N := X_1 + ··· + X_N is said to have the binomial distribution Binom(N, p).
source_evidence.observation: For fixed p ∈ (0,1), the first N variables of the inherited i.i.d. Ber(p) sequence are summed using one-based indexing, and the source asserts that this sum has law Binom(N,p). The standardized convergence in Equation (1.7) is a later central-limit-theorem consequence, not part of this definition.

binders: (X_i)_{i≥1}, a one-based sequence of random variables
S_N, the sum of the first N variables
hypotheses: The sequence (X_i)_{i≥1} is independent and identically distributed.
conclusions: S_N has the binomial distribution Binom(N,p).
definitions_and_conventions: X_i ∼ Ber(p) means that X_i takes value 1 with probability p and value 0 with probability 1-p.
The sum uses one-based indexing and contains exactly N terms.
The phrase 'has the binomial distribution Binom(N,p)' is an assertion about the law of S_N, not a pointwise equality of random variables.
implicit_context: The i.i.d. condition is inherited from the central limit theorem setup rather than repeated in the binomial-law sentence.
The same fixed parameter p is used for every X_i and does not vary with i or N.
The displayed finite sum implicitly treats N as positive.
Equation (1.7), asserting standardized convergence to the normal distribution as N → ∞, is a subsequent CLT/de Moivre-Laplace result and is excluded from the binomial definition.

details: Their common law is Ber(p) for one fixed p ∈ (0,1).
The recalled mean is p and variance is p(1-p).
S_N contains the first N variables.
The indices run from 1 through N.
The law of S_N is Binom(N,p).
Independence and the common Ber(p) law are essential premises.
The binomial-law assertion is the target definition at this locus.
The asymptotic normal convergence in Equation (1.7) is not part of the definition.
No central-limit or de Moivre-Laplace conclusion belongs in this target.

undebatable_constraints: Require p to lie strictly between 0 and 1.
Use one fixed p for the entire sequence.
Retain both independence and identical Ber(p) distribution of the X_i.
Define S_N from the first N variables with one-based indices 1 through N.
Assert that the law of S_N is Binom(N,p).
Do not weaken equality in law to a statement based only on matching moments.
Do not interpret Binom(N,p) as pointwise equality with a distinguished random variable.
Do not include the Equation (1.7) normal-limit statement in HDP-01-DEF-BINOMIAL.

contract_plain_english: Fix p strictly between 0 and 1 and take an inherited one-based i.i.d. sequence of Bernoulli(p) random variables. For a positive integer N, sum exactly X_1 through X_N and call the result S_N. The required assertion is that S_N has distribution Binom(N,p). Bernoulli(p) uses values 1 and 0 with probabilities p and 1-p, respectively, with mean p and variance p(1-p). The later standardized normal-limit statement in Equation (1.7) is explicitly outside this contract.
